## Overview

[SDRF](https://github.com/bigbio/proteomics-metadata-standard) (Sample and Data
Relationship Format) describes samples, assays, and data files for proteomics
deposition. OlinkAnalyze supports the **affinity-proteomics** template with
three related functions:

| Function | Role |
|----------|------|
| `olink_sdrf()` | Build SDRF from long-format **NPX** (+ optional sample metadata) |
| `generate_sdrf()` | Build SDRF from a **sample metadata** table only (e.g. `manifest`) |
| `olink_sdrf_validate()` | Soft-dependency check via Python `sdrf-pipelines` (`parse_sdrf`) |

Column expectations come from the package YAML under
`OlinkAnalyze/data-raw/sdrf/` (`base` → `sample-metadata` →
`affinity-proteomics`), stored internally as `sdrf_column_dict`.

This document mirrors the smoke script `example_sdrf.R`, with more explanation
of each step. Run it from the **repository root** (the folder that contains
`OlinkAnalyze/`).

::: {.callout-note}
## Optional validation

Writing an SDRF file does **not** require Python. Validation
(`validate = TRUE`) calls `olink_sdrf_validate()`, which needs
`parse_sdrf` on `PATH`:

```bash
pip install "sdrf-pipelines[ontology]"
```

If it is missing and `validate_error = FALSE`, validation is **skipped** with
a warning (`skipped = TRUE` in the result list).
:::

```{r}
#| label: setup
pkg_dir <- "OlinkAnalyze"
if (!dir.exists(pkg_dir)) {
  stop("Open / render this document from the repo root (folder with OlinkAnalyze/).")
}
devtools::load_all(pkg_dir, quiet = TRUE)
```

## A. `olink_sdrf()` — from NPX and sample metadata

### When to use it

Use `olink_sdrf()` when you already have long-format NPX (e.g. from
`read_npx()` or package data `npx_data1`). It:

1. Resolves the sample ID column via `column_name_dict` aliases  
2. Optionally joins `sample_metadata` on that ID  
3. Writes required affinity-proteomics headers (sample type, organism, platform, …)  
4. Maps leftover metadata columns to `characteristics[<name>]`  
5. Labels SampleIDs matching `CONTROL|CTRL` as `plate control`

::: {.callout-important}
## `manifest` vs `npx_data1`

Package datasets `manifest` and `npx_data1` do **not** share SampleIDs. For this
example we build `sample_metadata` from columns already on `npx_data1`.
:::

```{r}
#| label: olink-sdrf-prepare
npx <- OlinkAnalyze::npx_data1

sample_metadata <- npx |>
  dplyr::distinct(
    SampleID,
    Subject,
    Treatment,
    Site,
    Time,
    Project
  )

list(
  npx_rows = nrow(npx),
  unique_samples = dplyr::n_distinct(npx$SampleID),
  metadata_rows = nrow(sample_metadata),
  overlap_with_manifest = length(
    intersect(unique(npx$SampleID), unique(OlinkAnalyze::manifest$SampleID))
  )
)
```

### Call

Important arguments:

- `npx` — long NPX table  
- `sample_metadata` — one row per sample (optional)  
- `platform` — e.g. `"Olink Target 96"`, `"Olink Explore HT"`  
- `organism` / `organism_part` — defaults `"homo sapiens"` / `"blood"`  
- `file` — path to write `*.sdrf.tsv` (required for on-disk validation)  
- `validate` — run `olink_sdrf_validate()` after write  

```{r}
#| label: olink-sdrf-run
out_npx <- file.path(getwd(), "smoke_olink.sdrf.tsv")

sdrf_npx <- olink_sdrf(
  npx = npx,
  sample_metadata = sample_metadata,
  file = out_npx,
  data_file = "npx_data1.tsv",
  platform = "Olink Target 96",
  organism = "homo sapiens",
  organism_part = "blood",
  validate = TRUE,
  validate_error = FALSE,
  skip_ontology = TRUE
)

utils::head(sdrf_npx, 3L)
```

```{r}
#| label: olink-sdrf-validation
validation_npx <- attr(sdrf_npx, "sdrf_validation")
if (is.null(validation_npx)) {
  message("No validation attribute (parse_sdrf missing, or validate = FALSE).")
} else {
  validation_npx[c("ok", "status", "skipped", "template", "sdrf_file")]
}
```

## B. `generate_sdrf()` — from metadata only

### When to use it

Use `generate_sdrf()` when you have a **sample plate map / study metadata**
table but no NPX yet (or you only need sample-level SDRF). The package
`manifest` dataset is a good example: `SubjectID`, `Visit`, `SampleID`, `Site`.

It:

1. Requires a sample ID column (`sample_id = "SampleID"` by default)  
2. Sets Olink platform via `get_all_olink_platforms()` short or full names  
3. Optionally sets `comment[panel name]` from a constant or a metadata column  
4. Turns **all other** metadata columns into `characteristics[<column>]`  
5. Uses `SubjectID` / `Subject` for `characteristics[biological replicate]` when present  

```{r}
#| label: platforms
get_all_olink_platforms()
```

```{r}
#| label: manifest-preview
manifest <- OlinkAnalyze::manifest
utils::head(manifest, 5L)
```

### Call (Target 96)

```{r}
#| label: generate-sdrf-target96
out_manifest <- file.path(getwd(), "smoke_manifest.sdrf.tsv")

sdrf_manifest <- generate_sdrf(
  metadata = manifest,
  sample_id = "SampleID",
  platform = "Target 96",
  panel_name = "Inflammation",
  organism = "homo sapiens",
  organism_part = "blood",
  file = out_manifest,
  data_file = "manifest_study.tsv",
  validate = TRUE,
  validate_error = FALSE,
  skip_ontology = TRUE
)

colnames(sdrf_manifest)
utils::head(sdrf_manifest, 3L)
```

Leftover `manifest` columns appear as characteristics, for example
`characteristics[SubjectID]`, `characteristics[Visit]`, and
`characteristics[Site]`.

```{r}
#| label: generate-sdrf-validation
validation_manifest <- attr(sdrf_manifest, "sdrf_validation")
if (is.null(validation_manifest)) {
  message("No validation attribute.")
} else {
  validation_manifest[c("ok", "status", "skipped", "template")]
}
```

### Same metadata, Explore HT panel

`platform` accepts short names from `get_all_olink_platforms()` or full names
such as `"Olink Explore HT"`.

```{r}
#| label: generate-sdrf-explore-ht
out_ht <- file.path(getwd(), "smoke_manifest_explore_ht.sdrf.tsv")

sdrf_ht <- generate_sdrf(
  metadata = manifest,
  platform = "Explore HT",
  panel_name = "Explore 1536",
  file = out_ht,
  validate = TRUE,
  validate_error = FALSE
)

unique(sdrf_ht[["comment[platform]"]])
unique(sdrf_ht[["comment[panel name]"]])
isTRUE(attr(sdrf_ht, "sdrf_validation")$ok)
```

## C. `olink_sdrf_validate()` — check a written file

You can validate any SDRF TSV independently (not only files just written by
the create helpers):

```{r}
#| label: validate-standalone
if (!nzchar(Sys.which("parse_sdrf"))) {
  message("parse_sdrf not on PATH — skipping standalone validate demo.")
} else {
  res <- olink_sdrf_validate(
    sdrf_file = out_manifest,
    template = "affinity-proteomics",
    skip_ontology = TRUE,
    error = FALSE
  )
  print(res[c("ok", "status", "skipped", "template")])
}
```

If `parse_sdrf` is missing, `olink_sdrf_validate(..., error = FALSE)` warns that
validation was skipped and returns `skipped = TRUE`.
